identity_reason: a layout primitive only places other components and has no look of its own to derive
concept: Center puts one part in the middle of the room it is given, on one axis or both, so a lone display or key sits in a fixed place like a lamp in the middle of a panel.

root.why: A centred part keeps one fixed position inside its box, so the layout does not reflow between states.

a-both.why: Centring on both axes puts a lone part, such as an empty-state mark, at the middle of its box and holds it there.

a-inline.why: Centring along the line only keeps the top edge fixed, so a part never jumps vertically when its neighbours change.

a-block.why: Centring from top to bottom only keeps the start edge on the inset line while the part sits at mid height.

s-sm.why: The narrowest cap holds one short line or a single key in the middle of a phone-wide column.

s-md.why: The tablet cap keeps a centred note or form at a width the eye scans without hunting for the next line.

s-lg.why: The laptop cap holds a centred unit with room either side so it reads as the only thing on the panel.

s-xl.why: The wide cap matches the page width, so a centred part lines up with the Container above it.

s-2xl.why: The widest cap stops a centred part from drifting far from its neighbours on large screens.
